scope: Theorem 2.4 (Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł) of the manuscript “A rational obstruction to strong chromatic splitting at height three” (preprints/A-rational-obstruction-to-strong-chromatic-splitting-at-height-three-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6d0bd23f35dc42a1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For 0 ≤ j ≤ d there are compatible GLd+1(Qp) × Gal(Qp/Qp)-equivariant isomorphisms of groups Hj int(Ωd C)(j) ≃ Spj(Zp)∗ , Hj ét(Ωd C, Fp(j)) ≃ Spj(Fp)∗ . Here Spj is the generalized Steinberg representation of [11, §4.1], the star denotes its continuous coefficient-linear dual with weak topology, and the right sides have trivial Galois action. These groups vanish for j > d, and H0 int(Ωd C) = Zp by constants. In particular, on the untwisted integral group in degree j, an arithmetic Galois element γ acts by χcyc(γ)−j.
